messages:
lee: Quick heads-up: during a staggered maintenance we saw a cold prefix for tenant=delta rehydrate on two owners and a pair of apply logs. low blast radius but correctness concern.

nora: Can you paste the snippet? my mental model says ownership flip while rehydrate was inflight.

lee: snippet: ```[2026-04-01T04:12:07Z] tenant=delta prefix=user-77 apply=ok node=shard-A
[2026-04-01T04:12:07Z] tenant=delta prefix=user-77 apply=ok node=shard-B```

ben: yep that's handoff vs rehydrate race. Two mitigation axes: tighten handoff (fence/ack) or make applies idempotent at the consumer layer. both have costs.

nora: other dimension: eviction interplay. If we treat cold prefixes as eviction candidates, a sudden rehydrate+handoff increases churn and widens the double-apply window. Maybe we should special-case recently-evicted prefixes with a stricter handshake.

lee: idea: add an eviction_epoch token on prefix metadata. On handoff, previous owner includes epoch in the handshake; new owner rejects rehydrates whose epoch doesn't match current ownership (or enters a slow-path requiring sequencer arbitration).

ben: that gives us a causal fence without lengthening global drain time. downside: more state in handshakes and potential reject loops on transient metadata lag.

nora: counterproposal: emit a short-lived rehydrate_lock when a cold prefix starts streaming data. The lock prevents ownership commit until either rehydrate completes or a timeout elapses. Ops can tune timeout. Simpler but might block some fast failovers.

lee: operational tradeoffs: longer locks reduce risk but hurt failover speed. Epoch tokens prefer availability but require strict metadata propagation.

ben: practical path: 1) add rehydrate telemetry tags (reason=eviction|handoff|failover, lock_latency_ms) + alert on handoff-after-rehydrate spikes; 2) implement eviction_epoch token RFC for medium-term; 3) add a canary ops flag to enable rehydrate_lock for suspect prefixes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling-upgrade shard-A -> shard-B completed 04:20 UTC :white_check_mark:

nora: I'll draft the RFC describing eviction_epoch handshake, failure modes, and a sim-case for duplicate-apply. lee will own a small telemetry PR. ben will prototype the rehydrate_lock as an ops-toggle.

lee: thanks. filing incident note and tagging SRE for ops flag canary. Closing follow-up RFC expected next week.
